atoms.sound: Today’s debate topic is on the effects of social media. First, each student will present an opening statement, then you will respond to each other’s ideas. Finally, you will give your concluding statements. Droove, you may start.
In my opinion, social media has more negative effects than positive ones. My main concern is how quickly misinformation spreads online and how easily it can influence people’s decisions.
In contrast, I believe social media can be positive. It helps people stay connected with friends and family and can also provide emotional support during difficult times.

I understand that social media helps people connect, but its risks are more serious. When false information spreads widely, many users accept it without checking reliable sources. This can affect important decisions about health, politics, and other major issues.

That is a fair concern, but misinformation is not only a problem with social media. People have always shared incorrect information. Social media can also spread helpful information quickly, such as news updates or support during emergencies.
The difference today is the speed and scale. Online posts can reach thousands of people within minutes. When false information spreads that quickly, it becomes much harder to correct.
That is why digital literacy is important. Users need to learn how to question sources and think critically about what they read. That way social media would be a useful tool rather than a problem.

In conclusion, while social media offers benefits, the spread of misinformation remains a serious challenge. Until users become better at recognising false information, the risks will continue to affect many people.

In conclusion, social media is a powerful tool that can be used in positive ways. If people learn to use it responsibly and check their sources, it can strengthen communication and provide valuable support.
